sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Dealate) Entirely dark brown; head blackish brown, postclypeus pale brown, antennae yellow, pronotum rusty yellowish brown. Distance between ocellus and compound eye greater than its long diameter and less than twice its short diameter; interocular distance 1.22 mm; head width across the compound eyes 1.80 mm. Fontanelle narrow, slit-like, the region around the fenestra only slightly depressed. Posterior margin of the pronotum entire (not concave); meso- and metanotum roundly concave, the corners obtusely rounded.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head blackish brown; tergites, abdominal tergites and antennal segment 1 dark smoky brown; coxae, femora and the region of the head around the antennae rusty brown; tibiae, tarsi and the distal half of the antennae very pale yellowish brown; nasus concolorous with the head, or with an indistinct pale area at the apex, the nasus rather slender. Antennal segment 2 distinctly shorter than segment 3; head hairless, or with only one or two setae posterolaterally; head rather short, head-nasus index about 0.70; head length 1.75—1.85 mm, head width about 1 mm. All abdominal tergites with a row of stiff marginal setae.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements (mm). Dealate queen: head length 2.16, head capsule length 1.50, head width across the compound eyes 1.83, ocellus long diameter 0.20, fontanelle length 0.11, compound eye diameter 0.45, distance between the inner margins of the eyes 1.43, antennal segment 1 length 0.24, segment 2 0.15, segment 3 0.22, pronotum length 0.81, width 0.50. Soldier: head length 1.62, nasus length 0.57, head width 1.02, pronotum width 0.58, length 0.26, hind tibia length 2.15, head-nasus index 0.50. Only one colony is known, collected in 1923 by E. H. Taylor near Iwahig, Thumb Peak, Palawan Island, at elevations below 4500 ft, building small, very light carton nests on shrubs or lianas; there are no covered galleries above or below the nest, and together with its long legs and dark coloration this suggests that the species forages away from the nest.

note: Adapted from the species-level redescription by Light & Wilson (1936), original in English; the alate (dealate queen) and the soldier are described and measured. The species was originally described by Light (1930); this entry follows the 1936 redescription.
